1  Driving Condition-Aware Multi-Agent Integrated Power and Thermal Management for Hybrid Electric Vehicles  Hanghang Cui 1, Arash Khalatbarisoltani 1, Jie Han 2, Wenxue Liu 1, Muhammad Saeed 3, and Xiaosong Hu 1  1 Department of Mechanical and Vehicle Engineering, Chongqing University, Chongqing, China, 2 Department of Aeronautical and Automotive Engineering, Loughborough University, Loughborough, England 3 Department of Chemical Engineering, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai, China  Abstract: Effective co-optimization of energy management strategy (EMS) and thermal management (TM) is crucial for optimizing fuel efficiency in hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs). Driving conditions significantly influence the performance of both EMS and TM in HEVs. This study presents a novel driving condition-aware integrated thermal and energy management (ITEM) framework. In this context, after analyzing and segmenting driving data into micro-trips, two primary features (average speed and maximum acceleration) are measured. Using the K-means approach, the micro-trips are clustered into three main groups. Finally, a deep neural network is employed to develop a real-time driving recognition model. An ITEM is then developed based on multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (DRL), leveraging the proposed real-time driving recognition model. The primary objectives are to improve the fuel economy and reduce TM power consumption while maintaining a pleasant cabin temperature for passengers. Our simulation results illustrate the effectiveness of the suggested framework and the positive impact of recognizing driving conditions on ITEM, improving fuel economy by 16.14% and reducing TM power consumption by 8.22% compared to the benchmark strategy. Keywords— deep reinforcement learning (DRL), driving condition recognition, hybrid electric vehicles (HEV), integrated thermal and energy management (ITEM). 1-Introduction Developing new efficient energy vehicles is an important initiative to strengthen the transportation sector to tackle increasing concerns about global warming and reduce emissions. There are multiple candidates like electric vehicles (EVs), hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs), and fuel cell vehicles (FCVs) [1]. However, HEVs are seen as one of the most suitable options for transitioning to fully green transportation alongside 

2025 International Conference on Advanced Vehicle Powertrains 
2  EVs and FCVs. Energy management strategies (EMSs) have been developed to manage power allocation among the multiple power sources and can be categorized primarily into three groups: rule-based [2], optimization-based [3-7], and learning-based [8-10]. In addition to the EMS, thermal management (TM) of the engine, battery, and cabin has a critical impact that cannot be ignored. Although EMS and TM problems may seem like two independent challenges, in terms of fuel savings and components’ lifetime, both EMS and TMS are, in fact, highly coupled. Temperature significantly affects the components and TM’s power consumption, usually provided by battery, thereby affecting overall HEV power consumption, battery charge sustainability, and battery pack lifetime. Moreover, maintaining cabin, battery pack, and engine temperatures within their optimal ranges while minimizing fuel consumption and battery degradation is challenging. For instance, [11] presents a health-conscious predictive EMS and investigates the impact of battery electro-thermal-aging models on the EMS results. In another study, an EMS is suggested that considers the preheating of the battery packs in low-temperature driving scenarios [12]. To address the multi-physical and complex dynamics of the EMS and TM of the cabin, battery, and engine, integrated thermal and energy management (ITEM) is proposed in the literature as a valuable opportunity [13-15].

3  Driving conditions also play a crucial role in the performance of EMSs and TMs, and neglecting these conditions can lead to a decline in the effectiveness of EMS strategies in real-world driving scenarios. Driving cycles can be categorized based on various factors, including vehicle speed, acceleration, and jerk, using both unsupervised learning methods (such as K-means, fuzzy C-means, and kernel density estimation) and supervised learning methods (Bayesian estimation, K-nearest neighbors, and support vector machines). Several studies have integrated driving conditions with EMSs, including adaptive equivalent consumption minimization strategy, stochastic model predictive control, and deep reinforcement learning (DRL). Even though there have been successful investigations, the majority of previous strategies have focused on driving-aware EMSs while mostly overlooking the impact of driving conditions on TM performance, TM power consumption, and cabin temperature. To this end, this study proposes a novel driving-style-aware ITEM strategy, with specific attention to exploring the impacts on fuel economy, TM power consumption, and cabin comfort. Taking into account the recognized driving conditions, as shown in Fig. 1, a multi-agent DRL-based ITEM is proposed to simultaneously find the optimal power allocation policy and learn the impact of driving conditions on ITEM to improve fuel economy and cabin comfort temperature. Extensive simulation results validate the proposed driving condition-aware multi-agent DRL approach, demonstrating significant improvements in fuel economy and TM power consumption while keeping cabin temperatures within a comfortable range, compared to the benchmark strategy.  The remainder of this study is structured as follows: The power-split HEV powertrain modelling is detailed in Section 2. The driving condition recognition algorithm is presented in Section 3. Section 4 describes the driving style-aware DRL ITEM. Section 5 discussed the simulation results, followed by the conclusion. 2-HEV Powertrain Modelling The power-split HEV model, including electrical, mechanical, and thermal power loops as displayed in Fig. 2, provided by Autonomie, a simulation tool created by the Argonne National Laboratory. 𝑄̇, is the heat load by the heat transmission. 3-Real-Time K-Means Driving-Recognition This study proposes a real-time driving recognition model based on the K-means algorithm and deep neural network (DNN). Ten standard driving profiles are designated; among them, nine driving cycles are used for initial clustering, and one is considered the unseen profile. A fixed timestep is selected to divide the driving dataset, which includes the chosen nine standard driving cycles, into 505 micro driving cycles, each lasting 20 seconds. After the driving division step, two driving characteristic parameters (average speed and maximum acceleration) are selected to characterize each micro trip. The main reason for choosing only a limited number of features is that the direct clustering of the resulting characteristic parameter matrix does not lead to high data dimensions or a heavy computational burden. To determine the labels for each driving cycle, a K-means cluster analysis approach is utilized to cluster the micro trips into three categories.

9    Fig. 3. K-means clustering algorithm categorized the driving data into three primary clusters Fig. 4. Clustering results of the JN1015 standard driving cycle  The model first calculates the distance between the current input sample and each cluster center. Then, it classifies them according to the principle of minimum distance to obtain the cluster label, which indicates the recognized type of driving cycle or style. Fig. 3 presents the K-means clustering results. For better illustration, the cluster number for the JN1015 standard driving cycle is shown in Fig. 4. After obtaining the labeled micro trips using the K-means algorithm, a DNN was employed to build an instantaneous driving recognition model. The two features derived from the original driving data and the K-means clustering output are used as inputs to the DNN. The trained real-time DNN-based driving recognition model achieves high accuracy, around 90%, compared to the micro trips that are clustered solely using K-means. 4-Driving-Aware Energy and Thermal Management Formulation The DDPG algorithm is selected to efficiently learn the optimal ITEM actions. The proposed control strategy is composed of two DRL agents, cabin TM and EMS, which aim collaboratively to reduce fuel and TM units' power consumption while keeping cabin temperature as close as possible to a comfortable range. Ten standard driving profiles are considered in this investigation; among them, nine driving cycles are for the initial clustering and training of the DRL agent, and one is considered an unseen profile. Figure 5 displays the ITEM framework with and without the driving recognition information comparison results under the NYCC driving cycle and shows that driving-aware ITEM effectively keeps the final SOC around 0.65, which is very close to the initial value. By leveraging the real-time DNN driving recognition model, the suggested framework reduces fuel consumption by 16.14% compared to the version without driving recognition. Moreover, the cabin temperature is more stable than in the DRL without driving input, which infers that the passenger feels a more comfortable temperature based on the proposed driving conditions-aware ITEM strategy. In addition, the power consumption of the TM shows an 8.22% reduction compared with the strategy without driving recognition inputs. These results highlight that integrating the driving recognition model with ITEM successfully enhances the performance of both EMS and TM in HEVs.

Comparison of the results under NYCC: a) battery temperature, b) engine temperature, c) cabin temperature, d) SOC, e) SOH, f) fuel consumption Conclusion This study proposes a real-time driving-aware ITEM for HEVs. The driving recognition model is developed based on the K-means algorithm and the training of a DNN model. The co-optimization of the EMS and TM is formulated within the multi-agent DRL framework, with the main objectives of improving fuel economy and reducing TM’s power consumption while ensuring that cabin temperature remains within a comfortable range. In order to integrate the driving recognition model, the results are added as an extra input to the ITEM framework. The results highlight that considering the real-time driving recognition model for ITEM can decrease fuel consumption and TM power consumption while keeping the cabin in a comfortable range compared with the standard ITEM without driving information. structure.title: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Vehicle Powertrains
structure.summary: This partial document, from the 2025 International Conference on Advanced Vehicle Powertrains, describes a novel framework for integrated power and thermal management (ITEM) in hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs). The framework is designed to be aware of driving conditions, which are analyzed and segmented into micro-trips. Key features like average speed and maximum acceleration are used to cluster these micro-trips into three groups using K-means. A deep neural network then develops a real-time driving recognition model. This model is leveraged by a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (DRL) approach to create the ITEM strategy. The main objectives are to enhance fuel economy, reduce thermal management power consumption, and maintain cabin comfort. Simulation results indicate significant improvements, with a 16.14% increase in fuel economy and an 8.22% reduction in thermal management power consumption compared to a benchmark strategy. The document highlights the importance of recognizing driving conditions for optimizing HEV performance.

structure.title: Driving Condition-Aware Multi-Agent Integrated Power and Thermal Management for Hybrid Electric Vehicles
structure.summary:
This partial document, from the 2025 International Conference on Advanced Vehicle Powertrains, introduces a novel "driving condition-aware integrated power and thermal management (ITEM)" framework for Hybrid Electric Vehicles (HEVs). The main points covered are:

*   **Problem Statement:** Optimizing fuel efficiency in HEVs requires effective co-optimization of energy management strategy (EMS) and thermal management (TM), as both are significantly influenced by driving conditions. Existing strategies often overlook the impact of driving conditions on TM performance and cabin comfort.
*   **Proposed Solution:** A new framework that integrates EMS and TM, making it aware of driving conditions. This involves:
    *   Segmenting driving data into micro-trips.
    *   Extracting key features like average speed and maximum acceleration.
    *   Clustering micro-trips into three main groups using K-means.
    *   Developing a real-time driving recognition model using a deep neural network (DNN).
    *   Creating an ITEM strategy based on multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (DRL), utilizing the driving recognition model.
*   **Objectives:** To improve fuel economy, reduce TM power consumption, and maintain a pleasant cabin temperature.
*   **Results:** Simulation results show significant improvements, with a 16.14% increase in fuel economy and an 8.22% reduction in TM power consumption compared to a benchmark strategy.
*   **Structure of the Paper:** The document outlines the subsequent sections covering HEV powertrain modeling, driving condition recognition, the DRL-based ITEM, and simulation results.
*   **HEV Powertrain Model:** Briefly describes the power-split HEV powertrain model, including electrical, mechanical, and thermal loops, and mentions the use of the Autonomie simulation tool.

structure.title: HEV Powertrain Modelling
structure.summary:
This partial document, from the 2025 International Conference on Advanced Vehicle Powertrains, focuses on a novel driving-style-aware Integrated Thermal and Energy Management (ITEM) strategy for hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs). The core problem addressed is the insufficient consideration of driving conditions' impact on both energy management systems (EMSs) and thermal management (TM) performance, leading to suboptimal real-world effectiveness.

The document proposes a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (DRL) based ITEM strategy that simultaneously optimizes power allocation and learns the influence of driving conditions on fuel economy and cabin comfort. It highlights the importance of driving condition recognition, mentioning both unsupervised and supervised learning methods.

The document then delves into the technical details of the proposed system:

*   **HEV Powertrain Modelling:** It describes a power-split HEV model using Autonomie, detailing the components like electric motors, the internal combustion engine (ICE), and their interconnections. It provides equations for calculating driving forces, resistances, requested power, and torques within the power-split system.
*   **Battery Modelling:** The battery power calculation, its equivalent circuit model (first-order RC), and the formulation for terminal voltage, polarization voltage, and cell current are presented. It also covers the state-of-charge (SOC) change calculation and a thermal model for battery cell temperature, including heat generation and cooling mechanisms. Furthermore, it details a semi-empirical aging formula to model battery capacity degradation and calculate the state-of-health (SOH).
*   **Engine Coolant and Cabin Temperature Modelling:** Equations are provided for the engine's coolant temperature, considering various heat generation and transfer components. The cabin temperature model is also described, incorporating heat flow from the climate control system, solar radiation, convection, and transmission.
*   **Real-Time Driving Recognition:** A specific section outlines a real-time driving recognition model using K-means clustering and deep neural networks (DNNs). It explains the process of dividing driving datasets into micro-cycles, selecting characteristic parameters (average speed and maximum acceleration), and clustering these micro-trips into categories.

structure.title: Real-Time K-Means Driving-Recognition
structure.summary:
This partial document, from the 2025 International Conference on Advanced Vehicle Powertrains, covers two main topics:

1.  **Thermal Modeling of Internal Combustion Engines (ICE) and Cabin Temperature:** It presents mathematical models for heat transfer within an ICE, detailing heat generation from fuel, conversion to work, and losses through exhaust, convection, coolant, cabin transfer, and heat storage. It also models cabin temperature dynamics, considering heat flow from the climate control system, solar radiation, convection from the roof and window, and heat transmission.

2.  **Real-Time Driving Recognition and Energy Management:**
    *   **Driving Recognition:** A real-time driving recognition model is proposed using K-means clustering and Deep Neural Networks (DNN). The approach involves dividing driving data into micro cycles, extracting characteristic parameters (average speed and maximum acceleration), clustering these micro cycles into categories using K-means, and then using a DNN to classify driving styles with high accuracy.
    *   **Energy and Thermal Management:** A control strategy is outlined for integrated energy and thermal management (ITEM) using the DDPG algorithm. This strategy employs two Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) agents (cabin thermal management and energy management system) to collaboratively minimize fuel and power consumption while maintaining a comfortable cabin temperature. The state space for the cabin agent is defined by cabin temperature, error, vehicle speed, and other factors.

structure.title: Driving-Aware Energy and Thermal Management Formulation
structure.summary: This partial document from the 2025 International Conference on Advanced Vehicle Powertrains discusses a driving-aware Integrated Energy and Thermal Management (ITEM) system for hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs). The system utilizes a K-means clustering algorithm to categorize driving data into distinct clusters, which are then used to train a Deep Neural Network (DNN) for real-time driving recognition. This recognized driving condition is incorporated into an ITEM formulation that employs two Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) agents: one for cabin thermal management (TM) and another for the energy management system (EMS). The cabin agent aims to maintain a comfortable cabin temperature by controlling the heater and AC, while the EMS agent optimizes the internal combustion engine (ICE) output power to reduce fuel consumption and sustain battery State of Charge (SoC). The document details the state and action spaces, as well as the reward functions for both DRL agents. Results show that the driving-aware ITEM strategy significantly reduces fuel consumption (16.14%) and TM power consumption (8.22%) compared to a system without driving recognition, while also improving cabin temperature stability and passenger comfort.

structure.title: Results and Discussion
structure.summary:
This partial document from the 2025 International Conference on Advanced Vehicle Powertrains discusses a "driving-aware ITEM" (likely an Energy Management Strategy) for Hybrid Electric Vehicles (HEVs). The main points covered are:

*   **A novel driving-aware ITEM framework:** This framework integrates a real-time driving recognition model (developed using K-means and a DNN) into the ITEM strategy.
*   **Performance assessment:** The document presents results comparing the driving-aware ITEM with a standard ITEM without driving recognition.
*   **Key improvements:** The driving-aware ITEM demonstrates significant benefits, including:
    *   Reduced fuel consumption (16.14% reduction).
    *   More stable cabin temperature, leading to increased passenger comfort.
    *   Reduced power consumption of the Transmission (TM) (8.22% reduction).
    *   Effective maintenance of the State of Charge (SoC) around the initial value.
*   **Methodology:** The co-optimization of the Energy Management System (EMS) and TM is formulated within a multi-agent Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) framework.
*   **Conclusion:** The study concludes that integrating real-time driving recognition significantly enhances the performance of both EMS and TM in HEVs, leading to improved fuel economy, reduced TM power consumption, and better cabin comfort.

structure.title: Conclusion

The strategy utilizes a K-means algorithm and a Deep Neural Network (DNN) for driving recognition, and a multi-agent Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) framework for co-optimizing the Energy Management System (EMS) and Thermal Management (TM). The primary objectives are to improve fuel economy and reduce TM power consumption while maintaining cabin comfort. The study demonstrates that incorporating real-time driving recognition into the ITEM framework leads to significant improvements, with a 16.14% reduction in fuel consumption and an 8.22% reduction in TM power consumption compared to standard ITEM methods that do not consider driving information.
